data.gender_notes: Premshankar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Prem (Love) + Shankar (Shiva). The name Premshankar carries the meaning “Love, before Shiva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Premshankar usually hope their child will grow to embody love, before shiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Premshankar is a beautiful combination of love and devotion. It symbolizes the deep longing and attachment towards God, especially Lord Shiva.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Premshankar total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Premshankar is a beautiful blend of two powerful words from Hindu culture - Prem (Love) and Shankar (Shiva). In Hinduism, Shiva is known as the god of love and desire, represented by the symbol of a pair of intertwined serpents, signifying the union of Shiva and Parvati (Shiva's consort). The name Premshankar elegantly marries the essence of divine love, signifying the deep-rooted connection that love and spirituality hold in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Premshankar holds significant spiritual significance in Hinduism. Prem represents unconditional love, kindness, and warmth, embodying the selfless and caring nature of a person. Shankar symbolizes Shiva, the supreme deity, who represents the ultimate reality and consciousness of the universe. By combining Prem and Shankar, the name suggests that the individual possesses the divine quality of love and is deeply connected to the divine consciousness. It is a constant reminder of the importance of maintaining love in both personal relationships and spiritual practices.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Premshankar: Love (Prem) and God (Shankar) reside within. The divine union of love and devotion.
